text.p: Shares in Finnish insurer Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola fell on Monday as profit-takers emerged after sharp rises last week and as buying interest in the share faded, brokers said.
At 1225/1025 GMT Pohjola traded at 151.00 markka, down 7.00 markka or almost five percent, in fair 4.5 million markka trade.
"There was a rush to buy (Pohjola) on Friday, and now the situation has been reversed," one broker said. "Interest has faded."
Insurance shares rose sharply last week on continued talk of restructuring in the Nordic financial services industry.
Brokers said, however, that Pohjola's losses on Monday did not necessarily signal an end to the merger speculation that has fuelled Finnish insurance shares recently.
